note: GRATUS PATHWAYS. A model is a pattern; a pathway is a walk. Each one is a real thing somebody is going through, and what to do on which day. Statements are plain and the owner may refine any of them.

pathways.name: The First Thirteen
pathways.why: The shortest road from never having used this to holding a gift you could give somebody.

steps.do: Write one true thing and choose an emoji
steps.note: Small is correct. The bus being on time is a real day.

steps.do: Write again with the same emoji
steps.note: Two days in, it is Nurtured. That is the whole trick: the same one, again.
Five days. Notice that nothing punished you for the gap, if you had one.
Look at what you have written so far, all together. That is the point of a journal.
Open Give. Choose it, say who it is for, write why. Send the link.

pathways.name: The Thirty Day Gift
pathways.why: A birthday, an anniversary, a leaving day. Thirty days of having thought about one person, which no shop sells.

steps.do: Start a plant that is only for them
steps.note: Pick an emoji you associate with them and use it for nothing else.

steps.do: One line a day about them
steps.note: Not about the gift. About them: something they did, something they say, something you noticed.
You will have forgotten most of it. That is why this works.
Open Give and write why, properly. Take your time; it is the only part they read first.
The days go with it. They can plant it and it keeps growing in their garden.

pathways.name: The Hard Season
pathways.why: For grief, burnout, illness, or a season that is simply heavy. Built to be impossible to fail.

steps.note: Nothing here decays. Miss a week, miss a month: the garden is exactly as you left it.
On a bad day, three words is a day. On a very bad day, nothing is also fine.
One plant for the whole season. Watching one thing grow is steadier than scattering.

steps.do: Read it back at the month
steps.note: Not to judge it. To see that the days happened and you were there for them.

steps.do: Give it away when you are ready
steps.note: Or never. A plant can stay in your garden for years.

pathways.name: The Morning Ledger
pathways.why: One line before anything else, for three weeks. The oldest practice there is, with nothing to break.

steps.do: Write before you open anything else
steps.note: Before mail, before the feed. One line.
Gratus learns the hour you usually come and says so when you arrive in it.

steps.do: A week in, do not check a number
steps.note: There is no streak to look at. That is deliberate.
One for the morning, one for whatever the day turned out to be.
The calendar shows which days you wrote. It is a shape, not a score.

pathways.name: The Team Quarter
pathways.why: Instead of a slide about morale, arrive at the retro with thirteen days of noticing what went right.

steps.note: Not for the project. For the people.

steps.do: One line a day about something that went right
steps.note: Specific. A name, a thing they did.
Open Give and draft it. You will edit it four times; that is correct.
Read it out, then send the link. It carries the days, which is the part that lands.

steps.do: Start the next one the same day
steps.note: The second quarter is easier because the habit is already there.

pathways.name: The Giving Circle
pathways.why: A donation is a number in a ledger. This is the version where the project hears from a person.

steps.note: The Giveth door inside Gratus reads their live list.
Thirteen days of attention on why this, and not something else.

steps.do: Give on Giveth, in your own wallet
steps.note: Gratus never touches the money and never holds a key.
Your words, paired with the project and the transaction. The steward reads it.
When they write back, the seed in your garden opens and keeps their reply inside it.

pathways.name: The Quiet Line
pathways.who: somebody a friendship went quiet with
pathways.why: For a relationship that did not end, it just stopped. This is the slow way back.

steps.do: A plant for them, without telling them
steps.note: This part is only yours.

steps.do: One line a week is enough
steps.note: What you actually miss. Be specific; vague warmth is not useful later.
Not the gift. Just a message. The plant is the reason you thought to.
If the door opened, the gift says what the message could not. If it did not, you still have the month.

pathways.name: The Handover
pathways.why: Leave the way you would want somebody to leave you: with what you noticed, written down.

steps.do: A plant for the place, not the job
steps.note: The people, the room, the thing you built.

steps.do: One line a day for your last fortnight
steps.note: What you will actually miss, and who did what.
This is the thing they keep. Longer than you think is right.

steps.do: Give it on your last day
steps.note: To the person taking over, or to the team. It carries the fortnight with it.

pathways.name: The Newcomer
pathways.why: A new place is a lot of small unfamiliar things. Writing them down is how they become yours.

steps.note: The city, the street, the flat.

steps.do: One thing a day that was good here
steps.note: A shop, a walk, a person who was kind. Small on purpose.

steps.do: Add a second plant for a person
steps.note: By now there is usually one.
Three weeks of evidence that it is working, on the day it does not feel like it is.

pathways.name: The Long Thread
pathways.why: One plant, one year. Nothing here decays, so this is the only app where that sentence is literally true.

steps.do: Choose one emoji and never change it
steps.note: This is the whole discipline.
It is Ready to Give many times over. Do not give it. Keep going.
Read the calendar view. The shape of your year is on it.
Gratus will tell you, quietly, on the morning it happens.
